answer.explanation:
Caffeine (`Cn1c(=O)c2c(ncn2C)n(C)c1=O`) has a low predicted inhibition profile across all five CYP classifiers, with the highest model score on CYP2C19 but still low overall. Predicted scores / validation percentiles: CYP1A2 0.0357 / 0.3786, CYP2C9 0.0038 / 0.0588, CYP2C19 0.0420 / 0.0086, CYP2D6 0.0112 / 0.0093, CYP3A4 0.0001 / 0.0621. None were flagged outside the training distribution.

Closest measured training analogue returned by the label search for each enzyme was the same single analogue: `Cn1c(=O)c2c(ncn2CCO)n(C)c1=O` at similarity 0.6 with measured_label 0 (negative dataset label) in the training split. I kept model scores separate from observed assay labels: the model outputs are uncalibrated rankings, while the neighbour label is a processed binary dataset label from the training set and does not establish mechanism, general inactivity, or safety.

No additional evidence lookup was needed because you asked for model profile and measured training analogues only.

answer.explanation: Caffeine is predicted to be a very weak inhibitor across all five CYP endpoints, with the lowest score on CYP3A4. The model output for `Cn1cnc2n(C)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)c12` was: CYP1A2 0.0357, CYP2C9 0.0038, CYP2C19 0.0420, CYP2D6 0.0112, and CYP3A4 0.0001. None of these were outside the training distribution.
